drivingQuestion: Is an omer reaped by day valid?
outcomeNote: The contradiction is developed and resolved in the next unit

segments.he: נִקְצַר בַּיּוֹם – כָּשֵׁר. וְהָתְנַן: כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה כָּשֵׁר לִקְצִירַת הָעוֹמֶר, וּלְהַקְטִיר חֲלָבִים וְאֵבָרִים. זֶה הַכְּלָל: דָּבָר שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ כׇּל הַיּוֹם – כָּשֵׁר כׇּל הַיּוֹם, דָּבָר שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ בְּלַיְלָה – כָּשֵׁר כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If «it was reaped during the day,» it is «fit.» The Gemara asks: «But didn’t we learn» in a mishna (Megilla 20b): All mitzvot that must be performed at night may be performed anytime during that night. Therefore, «the entire night is valid» for «reaping the omer» on the night following the first day of Passover, «for burning the fats» of offerings that had been brought during the preceding day, «and» for burning «the limbs» of burnt offerings. «This is the principle: A matter that it is a mitzva» to perform «during the entire day is valid» if performed anytime during «the entire day,» and likewise «a matter that it is a mitzva» to perform «at night is valid» if performed anytime during «the entire night.»

edges.about: whether a night mitzva like reaping the omer is valid by day, given the Megilla mishna's parallel of night and day mitzvot

positions.claim: an omer reaped by day is fit
a night mitzva is valid all night; a day mitzva all day
